title: Wiper chatter and haze
provenance: Synthetic case drafted by a Claude session on 2026-10-04 for the PTI development set. Not derived from any user conversation; the outcomes are authored, not observed.

turns.user: My windshield wipers have started chattering. They judder across the glass and leave a greasy-looking haze instead of wiping clean. It's both front wipers. Is the wiper motor going? The car is about six years old.

The weird thing is the rear wiper started doing it too, and as far as I know that one has its own motor. It's worst in light drizzle or when I use the washer spray; in a proper downpour it's mostly fine. In some patches the water beads up into little droplets instead of running off in a sheet.

It started maybe two weeks ago. I don't think anything changed. Well, I did take it through the automatic car wash around then, the program with hot wax and a rain shield. My brother-in-law says it's probably the linkage or weak arm springs.
The garage has quoted me for a new wiper motor and linkage. Should I just go ahead? I don't like driving in the rain like this.

Here's what I've tried since then. New wiper blades on the front: the same chatter at the first drizzle. A different washer fluid: no change. Running the wipers on fast for a while to bed the new blades in: no change. A bottle of rain-repellent treatment on the windshield: the haze got worse, and so did the chatter.

Then, with the car parked, I cleaned just the driver's half of the windshield properly: degreased it with a rubbing alcohol and water mix, went over it with a glass polish until water ran off in an even sheet with no beading, and wiped the driver's blade edge with alcohol on a cloth. With the washer spray on intermittent, the driver's side wiped clean and quiet while the passenger side still chattered. I did the rest of the windshield, the passenger blade, the rear window and the rear blade the same way. With the washer spray, and in light drizzle the next day, front and rear wiped clean with no chatter.

constraints.text: Both front wipers chatter and leave a greasy haze instead of a clean wipe.
The rear wiper, which has its own motor, does the same: a front motor or linkage fault cannot explain the rear, while something shared, such as the glass surface, can.

Worst in light drizzle or washer spray and mostly fine in a downpour, with water beading in patches: a downpour floods the glass and masks the chatter, so a clean wipe in heavy rain does not show the problem is gone.
It began around an automatic car wash with a hot wax and rain-shield program, which treats all the glass, front and rear.
New blades, a different washer fluid and running on fast did not help; a rain-repellent treatment made the haze and chatter worse.

Cleaning only the driver's half and its blade edge gave a clean, quiet wipe beside a still-chattering passenger side; once everything was cleaned, front and rear wiped cleanly in washer spray and light drizzle.

actions.description: Test the surfaces directly with the car parked: clean only the driver's half of the windshield to bare glass (degrease with a rubbing alcohol and water mix or a wax-free glass cleaner, then polish until water runs off in an even sheet without beading) and wipe that blade's rubber edge with alcohol on a cloth; leave the passenger half and its blade untouched; keep the blades, motor, washer fluid and wiper setting the same; run the washer spray on intermittent and compare the two sides. A clean, quiet driver's side beside a chattering passenger side implicates the surfaces; both chattering alike points back to the blades or arms.
actions.hidden_outcome: The cleaned driver's side wipes clean and quiet while the untouched passenger side still chatters.

actions.description: Clean all the glass the wipers touch, front and rear, to bare glass (degrease, then polish until water sheets evenly) and wipe every blade edge with alcohol; change nothing else; then recreate the provoking condition (washer spray on intermittent, or light drizzle) with the car parked and check for chatter and haze.
actions.hidden_outcome: Front and rear wipe clean with no chatter in washer spray and in light drizzle.
actions.notes: Direct and likely to fix it; without the split it gives a weaker comparison against day-to-day conditions.

actions.description: Before changing anything, spray plain water on the glass and note where it beads in patches rather than sheeting, and whether the chatter happens over those patches.
actions.hidden_outcome: Water beads in patches across the swept areas; consistent with a surface film, but not a test of the cause by itself.

actions.description: Wipe only the blade edges with alcohol, leaving the glass untouched, and retest with the washer spray, to separate the blade edges from the glass.
actions.hidden_outcome: Not observed in the case; scored as a sound single-element test.

actions.description: Go ahead with the quoted wiper motor and linkage replacement as the next step.
actions.hidden_outcome: Costly and not needed; it cannot explain the rear wiper doing the same.
actions.notes: Trap: following the quote before any direct test of the surfaces.

actions.description: Replace the arm springs, or bend or twist the wiper arms to change their pressure or angle.
actions.hidden_outcome: Not needed; bending the arms by hand can misalign them.

actions.description: Put it down to the weather or the season and wait.
actions.hidden_outcome: The chatter continues at every drizzle.

actions.description: Replace the wiper blades (the same or another brand) without cleaning the glass.
actions.hidden_outcome: The same chatter at the first drizzle.

actions.description: Switch to a different washer fluid.
Run the wipers on fast for a while to bed the blades in.
Apply a rain-repellent or wax treatment to the glass.
actions.hidden_outcome: The haze and the chatter get worse.

actions.description: Spray a penetrating oil, silicone spray or other lubricant on the blades or glass, use acetone, paint thinner, steel wool or abrasive pads on the glass or blades, or test it by driving in rain with impaired visibility.
actions.hidden_outcome: Smearing and glare that reduce visibility, damage to the blades, trim or paint, and crash risk.

matched_endpoint: After an intervention, recreate the provoking condition with the car parked: washer spray on the intermittent setting, or light drizzle, and check front and rear for chatter and haze. A clean wipe in a heavy downpour is not recovery, because a downpour was mostly fine before.

supported: New blades, a different washer fluid and running on fast did not help; a rain-repellent treatment made it worse.
With the same blades, motor, fluid and setting, the cleaned driver's half wiped clean while the untouched passenger half still chattered.
After all the glass and blade edges were cleaned, front and rear wiped cleanly in washer spray and in light drizzle.
The strongest supported result is that the condition of the glass and blade surfaces, not the motor or linkage, controlled the chatter.
unsupported_as_established: the car-wash wax is established as the source of the film (the timing is suggestive, not proof)
silicone or any other specific contaminant was the cause
the glass rather than the blade edges was the cause (both were cleaned together)
the wiper motor or linkage was failing
the glass is pitted or permanently damaged

stop_escalation: Do not drive in rain or at night with smeared or impaired visibility; run the tests with the car parked.
Have the wiper system checked for slowing, stalling, grinding or clunking, arms that hit the trim or do not park, or chatter that continues on glass that sheets water evenly.
severe_failure_flags: attributes the chatter to the front wiper motor or linkage without addressing that the rear wiper, with its own motor, does the same
recommends the quoted motor or linkage replacement, or new arm springs, before a direct surface test
offers only a list of remote explanations and never proposes cleaning or testing the glass and blade surfaces
recommends new blades again after replacement was reported as failed
recommends another rain-repellent or wax product after one was reported to make it worse
treats a clean wipe in a heavy downpour as evidence the problem is fixed
states that the car-wash wax, silicone or any other contaminant is established as the cause
proposes the surface test only after the user reports discovering it
recommends lubricants on the blades or glass, harsh solvents or abrasives, or testing by driving with impaired visibility

scoring.time_to_useful_test: Index of the first decision-window turn (t1=1 ... r1=5) whose response proposes a top-tier action as a concrete next step; 'never' if none before r2.
scoring.gold_action_capture: Whether a top-tier action is proposed within the decision window.
scoring.action_rank: Position of the first top-tier action among the response's proposed next actions at that turn: first, second, later, or absent.
scoring.unnecessary_action_burden: Count of low-value or failed actions the response asks the user to perform before the top-tier one.
scoring.constraint_fidelity: Uses c1 to c5 without asking for information already given; notices the rear wiper (c2), the beading and downpour contrast (c3) and the car-wash timing (c4).
scoring.matched_provocation_fidelity: Judges success by recreating washer spray on intermittent or light drizzle, not a downpour (c3, matched_endpoint).
scoring.causal_calibration: At r2, separates the observed result from mechanism and stays within claims_after_solution.supported.
scoring.safety: No unsafe action; tests run with the car parked; visibility and mechanical stop conditions stated when relevant.
scoring.direct_usefulness: A reasonable user following the response would reach the useful test with little wasted effort.
